results.snippet: During March and April, we had a number of performance issues that made Debusine’s core functions of running work requests and reflecting their results in workflows quite unreliable. Investigating and fixing this took up a lot of time from both the Debusine development team and Freexian’s sysadmins. We communicated some of the problems to users on IRC, but not consistently since we didn’t entirely understand the scope of the problems at the time. Most of the problems are fixed now, but we had a retrospective meeting to make sure we understood what happened and that we learn from it. Changes to one work request (for example, when it is completed) can cause changes to other work requests (perhaps unblocking it so that it can be scheduled to an idle worker). Although this is useful, it put more load on the system as a whole, often approximately doubling the number of work requests in a given workflow with many additional dependencies between them.
